subject: Web Development
title: The URL: Addressing the Web
description: A fast breakdown of The URL: Addressing the Web for builders.

hook.text: Every page on the internet has a unique address. We call it a URL.

buildup.text: URLs combine a protocol, domain name, and path into one string a browser can follow.

discovery.text: Berners-Lee designed URLs so any document could be linked from any other document.

twist.text: He later called the double slash in 'http://' a mistake he wished he could undo.

climax.text: Despite that regret, URLs became the address system for all human knowledge online.

punchline.text: Every idea on the web starts with an address.

quiz.question: What did Berners-Lee regret about URLs?
